name: Problem Solver
description: Formula first, then two fully worked examples that increase in difficulty, then questions students try themselves. Built for maths, physics and any numerical topic.
audience: Teaching a method students must practise: numericals, derivations, accounting entries.

signals.why: your words ask for problem solving

slides.guidance: Lesson title for {topic} and a short subtitle that names the class level.
The method students will be able to apply for {topic}, as skills ('calculate…', 'identify…').
The core formula or rule of {topic} with every symbol explained and its unit.
A simple worked example for {topic}: one problem, each step with the reason, the final answer with unit.
A harder worked example for {topic} that adds one twist students often miss. Show the step where the twist is handled.
The most common mistake {grade} students make when solving {topic} and the correct way.

variants.guidance: A classroom meme about {topic}. Pick one format from MEME FORMATS that matches the idea, write captions a {grade} student finds funny and that make the correct idea easier to remember. Kind to students, never about a person.

slides.guidance: A problem for students to solve themselves. The wrong options are the answers produced by the common mistakes.
The method in three to five steps students can reuse.
